flags.name: Flag 1 - XSS
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, use the search bar to filter for XSS, and open any matching alert to read the name of the detection rule that raised it. Open an XSS alert. What is the name of the detection rule that raised it? The CF- prefix code is enough. The flag is the name of the detection rule.
flags.plainAnswer: CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score)

hints.description: Every rule we deploy is named CF-<s1-value>surface</s1-value>-<s1-value>attack</s1-value>.
The surface is the <s1-value>WAF</s1-value>; the attack is <s1-value>XSS</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>CF-WAF-XSS — Cross-Site Scripting against shop.soledrop.co (WAF ML score)</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 2 - XSS
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, open a CF-WAF-XSS alert, and read the Purple AI Overview panel. Which MITRE ATT&CK ID does this detection map to the Execution tactic? The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID

hints.description: Two techniques are listed; the other one, <s1-value>T1190</s1-value>, is <s1-value>Initial Access</s1-value>.
It is the JavaScript sub-technique of <s1-value>Command and Scripting Interpreter</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>T1059.007</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 3 - XSS - Workflow
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, open an XSS alert, and click the Automate button in the top right of the alert panel. HyperAutomation workflows allow Threat Hunters to enrich alerts, gather third-party threat intel, seek out determinitions from analysts, and conduct follow-up responses automatically whenever alerts are triggered. What is the name of the available workflow? The flag is the name of the workflow under Available Workflows

hints.description: It is one of the CF-* playbooks deployed into your site.
It handles all three WAF web attacks — SQLi, XSS and traversal — from one playbook.
The flag is <s1-answer>CF-WAF-WebAttack</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF Integration
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Hyperautomation and open the CF-WAF-WebAttack workflow. Its actions run top to bottom, in order — scroll through them to find the first block that uses a Cloudflare integration. What is the name of the first block that uses the Cloudflare integration? The flag is the name of the Cloudflare integration.

hints.description: Skip the Trigger, Set Context, Create Power Query and Extract Enrichment — none use Cloudflare.
It is a best-effort enrichment read that fetches Cloudflare's own IP ranges.
The flag is <s1-answer>CF JD Cloud IP Details</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Workflow Conditional
flags.description: Still in that same workflow, find the Cloudflare action named CF Ruleset Host Block, which sits immediately before the Response Had Failure condition, open it, and read its JSON request body. Find the action labeled CF Ruleset Host Block. This action has already ran. Look in the Body section to see the JSON body that was returned. What action was taken? The flag is the value of the action field.

hints.description: Put another way: what is the value of the <s1-value>action</s1-value> field in that body?

The body is a small JSON object with <s1-value>action</s1-value>, <s1-value>expression</s1-value>, <s1-value>description</s1-value> and <s1-value>enabled</s1-value> — and it is the most decisive thing a WAF rule can do.
The flag is <s1-answer>Block</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - CF Block IP
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Still in the same workflow, open the <s1-value>Cloudflare Block IP</s1-value> action and read the URL it calls.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
The access rule it creates — is it scoped to the whole account/user, or to a single zone?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the scope of the access rule.</s1-flag>

hints.description: Read the URL path segment right after /client/v4/.
The path contains /zones/id/ — an account-scoped rule would say /user/ instead.
The flag is <s1-answer>Zone</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Credential Stuffing
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, filter for Credential Stuffing, open an alert, scroll down to Rule Details, and read the group ... by clause at the end of the underlying PowerQuery. Each alert represents one attacker, not one request. Which field does the rule group by to make that true? The flag is the field.

hints.description: Look at the last line of the query's <s1-value>group ... by</s1-value> clause.
It is the attacker's address, aliased earlier in the query from <s1-value>src_endpoint.ip</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>src_ip</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 8 - Credential Stuffing
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, open a CF-Access-CredStuffing alert, and read the Purple AI Overview panel. Which MITRE ATT&CK ID does this detection associate with Password Guessing activity? The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID

hints.description: Both are sub-techniques of <s1-value>T1110</s1-value>, <s1-value>Brute Force</s1-value> — read the names, not just the numbers.
The other one, <s1-value>T1110.004</s1-value>, is associated with <s1-value>Credential Stuffing</s1-value>. You want <s1-value>Password Guessing</s1-value>.
The flag is <s1-answer>T1110.001</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 9 - VirusTotal
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Alerts, filter for Credential Stuffing, and sort by the Analyst Verdict column — the playbook's enrichment note only exists on an alert an analyst has already judged. Open one with a verdict, then open its Notes tab. The response playbook enriched the attacker IP against two reputation services. VirusTotal is one. What is the other? The flag is the other reputation service.

hints.description: The note lists each enrichment source on its own line with its verdict.
The second one reports an abuse confidence score rather than a vendor ratio.
The flag is <s1-answer>AbuseIPDB</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 10 - URL of target Site
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Stay on the <s1-label>Notes</s1-label> panel from the previous question and read the destination URL the playbook recorded.
</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>

What is the URL of the site being targeted?

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="____.soledrop.co">The flag is URL of the site being targeted.</s1-flag>

hints.description: It is in the same note you just read — the host the <s1-value>Credential Stuffing</s1-value> was aimed at.
It is the employee portal, not the shop and not the API.
The flag is <s1-answer>portal.soledrop.co</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 11 - Rule JSON Body
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Hyperautomation, open the workflow called See WAF Rule, click its Cloudflare action, and click Test Action. Use the magnifying glass in the output panel to search for Login. Look at the Test Output. What is the id of the firewall rule that logs all Login attempts? The flag is the id value.

hints.description:
Use Ctrl-F or the magnifying glass to find the section of the output mentioning logins.

The id is the very first field in that respective JSON body.
The rule's description mentions login POSTs; you want its id field, a 32-character hex string.
The flag is <s1-answer>7d4da0650add48ceaf5859040fe50edd</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 12 - CF Firewall Rules
flags.token: URI Path contains /login and Request Method equals POST
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, click Domains from the left-hand navigation and select the soledrop.co zone. Open the Security dropdown and choose Security Rules, then find the rule you just identified from the SentinelOne side and read the condition Cloudflare renders for it in the description column. Open that same rule in Cloudflare. What condition does the dashboard say it matches? The flag is the description.
flags.plainAnswer: URI Path contains /login and Request Method equals POST

hints.description: Cloudflare renders the raw expression in plain English on the rule row in the description column.
It is two conditions joined by 'and': one on the path, one on the method.
The flag is <s1-answer>URI Path contains /login and Request Method equals POST</s1-answer>.
